# claude-workman

> An open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI assistants human-mode control
> of a Linux desktop: it captures a screenshot, reads the AT-SPI2 accessibility tree, then moves
> the mouse, clicks, types, and switches windows. Clicks are addressed by element role and name
> rather than guessed pixel coordinates, so automation survives layout changes.

- Repository: https://github.com/AdvisorAGI/claude-workman
- License: MIT
- Language: Python 3.10+
- Platform: Linux / X11 (Wayland and macOS backends planned)
- Install: `pip install claude-workman`
- Run: `python -m workman.server` (stdio MCP server)
- Register with Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user workman -- python -m workman.server`

## What it is

claude-workman is desktop "computer use" for Linux, packaged as an MCP server so any MCP client
(Claude, Claude Code, and others) can drive a real desktop. It is not a browser automation tool:
it controls native applications, terminals, file managers and settings dialogs as well as
browsers.

## Key differentiator

It fuses two signals every turn — a screenshot and the AT-SPI2 accessibility tree — so an action
can be expressed semantically ("click the push button named Continue") and land on that element's
center. This is the Linux equivalent of macOS AXUIElement-based computer use. Pixel coordinates
remain available as a fallback.

## Tools

- `screenshot`, `screenshot_region` — capture the display or a sub-rectangle as PNG
- `accessibility_tree` — actionable elements as {app, role, name, x, y, w, h}
- `click_element` — find by role + name, click the element center (no pixel guessing)
- `enable_accessibility` — enable AT-SPI tree export, and stop the screen reader from speaking
- `list_windows`, `focus_window` — enumerate and raise windows
- `click`, `move`, `drag`, `scroll` — pointer actions
- `type_text`, `press_key` — keyboard input, xdotool key syntax
- `show_cursor` — visual click-cursor overlay (ring + ripple) for human oversight

## Requirements

xdotool (input), ffmpeg (x11grab screen capture), python3-gi + gir1.2-atspi-2.0 (accessibility
tree; the import is `gi.repository.Atspi`, not `pyatspi`). Pillow is optional (screenshot
downscaling); GTK 3 is optional (cursor overlay).

## Safety notes

- Enabling web-content accessibility for Chromium/Electron also causes the Orca screen reader to
  read the screen aloud; `enable_accessibility` stops Orca automatically (`pkill -x orca`).
- claude-workman does not solve CAPTCHAs and is not an anti-bot bypass tool.
- Treat it as handing over mouse and keyboard: use `show_cursor` for visibility and verify by
  screenshot before irreversible actions.

## Naming

Named after the Walkman — a small, portable thing that just plays.
